statute: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-59-10 et seq. (Residential Builders); S.C. Code Ann. § 29-5-10 et seq. (Mechanics' Liens)
license_label: South Carolina Residential Builder License / Specialty Contractor Registration Number
license_notes: A South Carolina residential builder license is required when the cost of the undertaking exceeds $5,000 (S.C. Code Ann. § 40-59-20). A residential specialty contractor license or registration is required when the undertaking exceeds $500. A specialty contractor may not construct residential additions without supervision by a licensed residential builder or other appropriately licensed person.

mandatory_clauses.label: Contractor license disclosure
Mechanics lien notice
mandatory_clauses.text:
NOTICE REGARDING MECHANICS' LIENS

Under South Carolina law, any person who furnishes labor or materials for the improvement of your real estate may be entitled to a mechanics' lien against that property if they are not paid. Where labor or material is furnished by someone employed by a contractor rather than by you directly, that person must notify you in writing of the labor or material furnished and its amount or value before the lien attaches. In no event may the aggregate amount of such liens exceed the amount you still owe under the contract price for the improvement. To protect yourself, obtain a lien waiver or release from each contractor, subcontractor, and material supplier before making final payment.

mandatory_clauses.label: Federal 3-day right to cancel (TILA)

penalties_for_non_compliance: A person or firm required to be licensed or registered who has not done so may not file a mechanics' lien or bring an action at law or in equity to enforce the contract (S.C. Code Ann. § 40-59-30). Engaging in residential building or specialty contracting without the required license or registration is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than $500 nor more than $10,000, imprisonment of not less than 30 days, or both.
notes: South Carolina requires a residential builder license above $5,000 and specialty contractor registration above $500. The unlicensed-contractor bar in § 40-59-30 is severe: it removes both lien rights and the right to sue on the contract, so license status should be confirmed before work begins. Section 29-5-40 conditions a lien by an indirectly-employed party on written notice to the owner. Federal 3-day TILA notice is used where the contract creates a lien on the buyer's primary residence.
